issues: Last week was very quiet and covers dropped sharply, with parents saying they were using the week to get children back into a school routine, so there were fewer families and more couples.
Delivery performance is inconsistent, with a different measure falling out of range each week; prep time was the problem last week and has now recovered.
Labour was inefficient because hours were cut hard on both front of house and back of house but the revenue did not come, and the rota structure is still seen as inefficient.
The general manager wants to review Jason's rota so that Ash can float between both areas and a back of house shift can be removed.
Jason is on holiday, so the general manager meeting will be held with Rohip after the call.

A one star review claimed there was plastic in the chicken laksa, but the dish was not on sale last week so the review is believed to be old; the team has been reminded to keep packaging plastic away from food.
A team member returns in two weeks, and a shortlist of CVs has been drawn up with trial shifts to be arranged.

The Chinese cooker was repaired but broke again the next morning with an ignition fault, and the contractor said it needs a service and a clean; there is a question over whether a second call out has to be paid for.
A B2B event runs this Saturday from 12 to 3, covered by the general manager and Harley.
The Leicester High Cross 35th birthday event is tea and coffee only and is not expected to affect trade.
The primary marketing material for Freshers has not yet arrived.
A two hour happy hour with two for one drinks has been proposed for Wednesdays, when both universities hold their social nights, to be promoted through B2B university connections.
Inka Cheung will visit the site on Friday afternoon or early evening before travelling on to Nottingham.

The remarketing campaign on Deliveroo and Slurp applies to this site, using scratch cards to convert delivery customers into dine in customers, with the launch postponed to the middle of next week or the week after while the design and print are finalised.

Region-wide (North England & Midlands): A new stock monitoring system has been introduced, using an API link to Kobas to send a daily email reminder each morning covering the main food items, with drinks to be added later.

Region-wide (North England & Midlands): The stock reminder system only works if sites stop blind matching in the store account and input every delivery on the day it is received, otherwise the reminders will be inaccurate.

Region-wide (North England & Midlands): Vouchers now have to be redeemed by the customer through the loyalty app rather than handed over at the till, which means event level discount codes can no longer be tracked.

Region-wide (North England & Midlands): The operational mindset is shifting away from cutting labour cost towards maximising revenue and profit, as constant cost cutting is burning staff out and damaging service and morale.

Region-wide (North England & Midlands): B2B event notes have been issued to sites and the staffing list for the Freshers Fair events is being finalised, so managers need to check their calendars and make sure enough manpower is arranged for those dates.
Region-wide (North England & Midlands): Unannounced site visits are expected at the end of the month, with Michael touring all sites and observing without warning, so standards need to be held.

Region-wide (North England & Midlands): The Deliveroo promotion includes a very limited number of one hundred per cent off bills, likely only one or two per site, and there is no cap on party size when one is redeemed.
